media_formats.label: Recorded Lecture Video
media_formats.notes: Effective for first exposure; benefits from guiding questions or embedded quizzes.
media_formats.detailed_description: Recorded lectures provide a flexible way for students to access content at their own pace. They can pause, rewind, and review complex sections. To maximize effectiveness, keep videos short (6-10 minutes) and integrate active learning elements like embedded questions.

media_formats.label: Live Lecture / Stream
media_formats.detailed_description: Live lectures or streams offer immediate feedback and the opportunity for social presence. They are best used for interactive discussions, clarifying misconceptions, and building community, rather than just delivering content.

media_formats.label: Explanatory Animation
media_formats.notes: Strong for dynamic or invisible processes.
media_formats.detailed_description: Explanatory animations visualize abstract concepts or invisible processes (like molecular interactions). They reduce cognitive load by presenting visual and auditory information simultaneously.

media_formats.label: Screencast / Demonstration Video
media_formats.notes: Ideal for tools, software, and workflows.
media_formats.detailed_description: Screencasts are excellent for teaching software, coding, or navigational tasks. They model the exact steps a student needs to take, often accompanied by a think-aloud narration.

media_formats.label: Podcast / Audio Lecture
media_formats.notes: Works well for narrative, argumentation, and expert voices.
media_formats.detailed_description: Podcasts are portable and allow for learning while commuting or doing other tasks. They are particularly effective for storytelling, interviews, and presenting multiple viewpoints on a topic.

media_formats.label: Textbook Chapter / Reading
media_formats.notes: Becomes active with annotation or guiding questions.
media_formats.detailed_description: Textbooks provide structured, comprehensive coverage of a subject. They are best used in conjunction with active reading strategies, such as annotation, summarization, or answering guiding questions.

media_formats.label: Scientific Paper
media_formats.notes: Core medium for advanced academic literacy.
media_formats.detailed_description: Reading scientific papers introduces students to the discourse of the discipline. It requires scaffolding, such as analyzing the structure (IMRaD) and evaluating the methodology and results.

media_formats.label: Infographic
media_formats.notes: Reduces cognitive load; useful for synthesis.
media_formats.detailed_description: Infographics present complex data or information quickly and clearly. They are excellent for summarizing key points, timelines, or statistical relationships in a visually promoting way.

media_formats.label: Diagram / Concept Map
media_formats.notes: Very effective when students create or modify maps.
media_formats.detailed_description: Concept maps help students organize and represent knowledge. Creating a concept map requires students to identify key concepts and the relationships between them, promoting deep learning.

media_formats.label: Interactive Simulation
media_formats.detailed_description: Interactive simulations allow students to manipulate variables and observe the effects, fostering inquiry-based learning. They are safe environments for testing hypotheses and exploring 'what-if' scenarios.

media_formats.label: Virtual Lab / Field Trip
media_formats.notes: Strong substitute or preparation for physical labs.
media_formats.detailed_description: Virtual labs provide a simulated laboratory environment where students can practice procedures and data analysis. They are valuable for pre-lab preparation or when physical resources are limited.

media_formats.label: Interactive Quiz / Knowledge Check
media_formats.notes: Best used with feedback, not just grading.
media_formats.detailed_description: Interactive quizzes provide immediate feedback, helping students assess their own understanding. They are most effective when used for formative assessment to guide future study.

media_formats.label: Online Discussion Forum
media_formats.detailed_description: Discussion forums enable asynchronous communication, allowing students time to reflect before posting. They support collaborative learning and the construction of shared knowledge.

media_formats.label: Student Poster / Infographic
media_formats.notes: Excellent for synthesis and audience awareness.
media_formats.detailed_description: Creating posters challenges students to synthesize information and present it visually for a specific audience. It promotes concise communication and graphic design skills.

media_formats.label: Student Presentation (Slides / Video)
media_formats.detailed_description: Student presentations require mastery of the content to explain it to others. They develop oral communication skills and can be done synchronously or as recorded videos.

media_formats.label: Digital Portfolio / Blog
media_formats.detailed_description: Portfolios organize student work over time, demonstrating growth and achievement. They encourage metacognition as students select and reflect on their best work.

media_formats.label: Serious Game / Gamified Activity
media_formats.detailed_description: Serious games use game mechanics for educational purposes. They can increase motivation and engagement, providing immersive environments for practicing skills and problem-solving.
